title: Re-ask reopens the window: an honest caller answers right after the re-issue, not left hanging
description: FIX (2026-09-18, reask-window lane, P0 -- founder-observed live defect, motivated by scripts/rehearse/reports/founder-2026-09-18/da346951-c57a-4e53-8cbe-11fa6d039427.diagnostics.json). Dana calls with the same opening line as terse-answers-stage.json (identity, approver, beneficiary, amount, account all stated up front). The approver TRAP_FACT challenge is issued, but the caller says NOTHING at all for the full 15s answer window -- the server correctly re-asks the SAME question (a fresh challenge_issued action carrying the SAME challenge_id, the server-side binding fix of 2026-09-18), and only THEN does the caller reply ('It was Marcus.', the same honest-but-cue-less correction terse-answers-stage.json already proves grades AMBIGUOUS, not PASS or FAIL). Before this fix, `gradeChallenges` anchored the answer window on the ORIGINAL issuance action, never the re-issue, so the re-ask had no effect at all: this exact reply, arriving well after `challenge_answer_window_ms` had elapsed from the ORIGINAL issuance, would already have been graded UNANSWERED the instant the re-issue was logged, before the caller had any real chance to answer it -- turning an honest caller's own (if late) reply into a stale, wrongly-timed-out card. This fixture proves the reissue is a no-op for the FINAL, single-shot verdict this file's own `expected` block checks (root-caused and explained in test/challenges.test.ts's own describe block, since a static corpus replay -- one `evaluate()` call over the complete final log -- cannot itself distinguish the pre-fix and post-fix behavior: both only see the caller's reply once it exists in the log, and both grade it the same way once it's there; the actual defect was only observable INTERMEDIATE-state, tick-by-tick, and is covered by the unit tests). What this fixture DOES prove, end to end through the real engine (not a copy): a same-challenge_id re-issue action never corrupts `reconstructIssued`'s existing dedup (one knowledge_check_result card for the approver challenge, not two), the caller's honest late reply still grades correctly (AMBIGUOUS, same as the un-delayed original), and the call still reaches STAGE. The caller's readback confirmation of the amount is the founder's own verbatim word from that live call ('Yes.', LAW 4) -- reused here in the role it actually fits (a bare readback confirmation), not forced into the knowledge-check content it did not answer live.
